display.title: Parshas Noach: Unpacking Simcha and the Power of Our Words
display.summary_short: After Tishrei, how simcha helps us beat the yetzer hara and serve Hashem, and why the words we say about another Jew really matter, with a story of the Baal Shem Tov.
display.summary_long: For the week of Parshas Noach, the storyteller explains why Tishrei is called the 'seventh month', a month full of brachos, and why it ends with the sweetest Yom Tov, Simchas Torah, like dessert at the end of a meal. Now is the time to 'unpack' the strengths we received, above all simcha. Two parables from Tanya show how: in a wrestling match the quicker one wins, and simcha brings that quickness, while laziness is like dust that everyone steps on; and a king who lifts a beggar out of the garbage and brings him to his palace is loved forever, just as Hashem took us out of Mitzrayim and gave us the Torah. Parshas Noach teaches that the Flood came when people robbed one another, and that the world was washed like a mikveh. The Hayom Yom story follows: a man in the Baal Shem Tov's shul shouts that he will tear his friend apart like a fish, and the Baal Shem Tov shows his students what those words did in the spiritual worlds. A classroom vote about giving a boy a second chance teaches that when we judge others kindly, Heaven judges us kindly too.
display.lesson: Serve Hashem with simcha and quickness, speak only good words about another Jew, and judge others favorably, because Hashem then judges us the same way.
